title: B2.3 Frontend Acceptance Closure
intent: Turn the B2 frontend into a deterministic, reviewable acceptance candidate by closing Storybook, end-to-end journey, test-stability, accessibility, bundle-budget, and evidence gaps.
scope: Align the Storybook toolchain, localize shared close controls, stabilize the known concurrency-sensitive UI tests, add an isolated Verrail acceptance journey and bundle baseline gate, and record complete verification evidence for the current B2 working tree.
non_goals: Implement WorkGraph, WorkNode, Stage, Review, Acceptance, or Temporal capability
Migrate inherited Issue data or remove compatibility routes
Redesign the B2 information architecture or visual system
Perform broad frontend performance optimization beyond establishing an explicit baseline budget
Commit, merge, deploy, release, or create a ship record without explicit approval
acceptance_criteria: Storybook packages use one compatible exact version and the static Storybook build succeeds.
A deterministic Playwright journey proves Project to Target to Work navigation at desktop and narrow-desktop viewports without uncaught page or console errors.
Shared Dialog and Sheet close controls expose localized accessible names while retaining keyboard dismissal and focus behavior.
The previously observed CompanyEnvironments, IssuesList, and cron-fires concurrency-sensitive tests pass under representative grouped and stable-suite execution.
A checked frontend bundle baseline prevents accidental growth beyond an explicitly recorded acceptance budget.
UI tests, typecheck, production build, token gates, brand gates, locale parity, Storybook, end-to-end acceptance, and diff checks pass or any unresolved gap is recorded truthfully.
Delivery receipt, evidence, acceptance mapping, screenshots, and an advisory review decision make the merge-readiness conclusion independently inspectable.
